title: the DSG mining where-to-mine and types

banner.title: The DSG MINING OPENER, WHERE TO MINE AND TYPES OF MINES, R519: printed pp. 48-49 (pdf 49-50) - the mining opener (the mined stones and metals as perhaps the most valuable of underground resources - copper and iron for blacksmithing, emeralds, rubies and gold prized - and the miner proficiency framework the DM may allow), the where-to-mine prospecting rules (the find-something chance equal to the Wisdom score plus the miner proficiency modifier, the no-yield regions of deep sand or dirt and hardened lava with the stream-traces exception, the Proficiency Check after a thorough search of at least a week covering about four miles square, the good conditions that forbid fending off bandits or hunting for food, the deep-snow impossibility, the thin-snow doubling or tripling, the rainstorm and rough-terrain and short-winter-daylight interferences with the DM extending the time, the repeat-search ladder of -1 and twice the time on the second search and -2 and tripled time on the third with corresponding increases and the automatic failure past a certain point, and the success reading Table 30: Mining Products), and the types-of-mines taxonomy (the placer and underground tunnel mines of a fantasy world, the strip mining excluded for its heavy equipment, the placer sifting of gravel, dirt, sand and water from a flowing stream needing only a shallow pan and patience, the eroded-vein streambed collection, the not-the-way-to-a-significant-lode limit, the tunnel mine trading more work for much greater wealth, and the book primarily ruling tunnel mining though placer mining remains possible along underground streams)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~6340-6465) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 66 = printed p. 49 holding the snow rules and the repeat-search ladder clean; the mining opener on the idx 65 tail) - every load-bearing number dual-confirmed: the Wisdom-score find chance, the one-week minimum search over four miles square, the deep-snow impossibility, the thin-snow double or triple, the -1/x2 and -2/x3 repeat ladder with the automatic failure, and the shallow-pan placer minimum. The DMG page 106 mining-rates seam (Table 27) and Table 30 are the NEXT round per the content-density rule: the mining chapter continues with excavating, vein direction Tables 28-29, shoring, and the products grids.
banner.sentinel: A prose round opening the mining chapter - no tables. The repeat-search modifiers pin as positive magnitudes with the minus in the name and comment per the R514 convention. The Wisdom-score chance and the miner-proficiency-modifier addition are pinned as prose booleans; the engine multiplies nothing - the search-time doubling and tripling pin as multipliers, not computed values. The Table 30 seam is noted for R520; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnmSearchMinWeeks
consts.comment: a thorough search of a possibly-yielding area requires at least a week of time under good searching conditions.

consts.name: dnmSearchAreaMilesSquare
consts.comment: the search generally covers an area about four miles square.

consts.name: dnmSecondSearchModifier
consts.comment: the second time an area is searched by any character with miner proficiency, the chances are rolled with a -1 modifier to the Proficiency Check (pinned as a positive magnitude with the minus in the name and comment).

consts.name: dnmSecondSearchTimeMult
consts.comment: twice as much time is required to search the area the second time.

consts.name: dnmThirdSearchModifier
consts.comment: if the attempt is made a third time, a -2 modifier applies to the Proficiency Check (pinned as a positive magnitude).

consts.name: dnmThirdSearchTimeMult
consts.comment: the third search takes tripled time; an area can be searched as many times as desired with corresponding increases in penalties.

bools.name: dnmMinedResourcesValuable
bools.comment: the stones and metals found by miners are perhaps the most valuable of all natural underground resources: strong metals like copper and iron for blacksmithing, valuable stones and metals like emeralds, rubies, and gold all highly prized.

bools.name: dnmMinerProficiencyFramework
bools.comment: with the miner proficiency (see the DSG Proficiency section) PCs may take an interest in mining; if the DM allows mining ventures, this section provides the framework governing the outcome of the enterprise.

bools.name: dnmFindChanceIsWisScore
bools.comment: as a general rule, a character with miner proficiency stands a chance equal to his Wisdom score (plus his miner proficiency modifier) of finding something of worth where he elects to dig.

bools.name: dnmNoYieldRegionsExist
bools.comment: certain areas do not yield anything of value regardless of the success of the proficiency roll: regions of deep sand or dirt, or areas of hardened lava.

bools.name: dnmStreamTracesException
bools.comment: streams flowing through no-yield regions might have brought traces of a valuable ore or a gemstone, but mining the ground itself is virtually guaranteed to yield nothing there.

bools.name: dnmCheckAfterThoroughSearch
bools.comment: if a miner seeks to mine an area the DM believes might yield valuable material, the character can make a Proficiency Check after thoroughly searching the area.

bools.name: dnmGoodConditionsRequired
bools.comment: good searching conditions mean the character cannot be fending off bandits or hunting for food while searching.

bools.name: dnmDeepSnowBlocksSearch
bools.comment: a deep snow cover makes such a search impossible.

bools.name: dnmThinSnowDoublesOrTriples
bools.comment: even a thin coating of snow doubles or triples the time needed to search an area.

bools.name: dnmAdverseConditionsDMExtends
bools.comment: steady rainstorms, rough terrain, and the short hours of daylight typical in wintertime can all interfere; the DM must decide how much additional time is required before the area is suitably searched.

bools.name: dnmFailedSearchRepeatable
bools.comment: if the Proficiency Check roll is unsuccessful, so is the search - but the character can repeat his search of the same area if he wants to, though the task grows more difficult.

bools.name: dnmAutoFailPastAPoint
bools.comment: after a certain point the modified Proficiency Check automatically fails, and further searches are fruitless.

bools.name: dnmSuccessReadsTable30
bools.comment: if the Proficiency Check succeeds, the miner has discovered something of value within the area searched - exactly what is determined by Table 30: Mining Products (the R520 seam).

bools.name: dnmPlacerAndTunnelTypes
bools.comment: the types of mines commonly encountered in a fantasy world include placer mines and underground (or tunnel) mines.

bools.name: dnmStripMiningExcluded
bools.comment: the strip mining common in the modern age requires heavy equipment not found in the typical AD&D game campaign.

bools.name: dnmPlacerSiftingOperation
bools.comment: placer mining involves sifting gravel, dirt, sand, and water from a flowing stream or river - most commonly employed above ground; at its most basic level the only requirements are a character with a shallow pan and a great deal of patience.

bools.name: dnmPlacerStreambedCollection
bools.comment: a placer mine gathers the mineral content of an underground vein of metal eroded by water and flowed downstream, collecting where the miner separates it from the water in the streambed.

bools.name: dnmPlacerNotSignificantLode
bools.comment: because only the mineral wealth eroded from the ground collects along the streambed, placer mining is not the way to discover a lode of significant value.

bools.name: dnmTunnelMoreWorkMoreWealth
bools.comment: an underground or tunnel mine requires a great deal more work than a placer mine, but the potential for wealth is much greater: a tunnel excavated into the earth, the dug rock examined for riches.

bools.name: dnmRulesPrimarilyTunnelMining
bools.comment: because the book deals solely with the underground, the mining rules deal primarily with tunnel mining - though placer mining is still possible along underground streams, underground characters and creatures are much more likely to labor in the lucrative tunnel mines.

examples.note: the search scale: at least a week under good conditions, covering about four miles square.

examples.expr: m['dnmSecondSearchModifier']() != 1 or m['dnmSecondSearchTimeMult']() != 2 or m['dnmThirdSearchModifier']() != 2 or m['dnmThirdSearchTimeMult']() != 3
examples.note: the repeat-search ladder: the second search at -1 and twice the time, the third at -2 and tripled time, with corresponding increases beyond.
